hypothesis: The ATR definition used to size the stop changes the result.
falsifierStatedBeforeRunning: To prefer one method the difference must hold the same sign in train, validate AND sealed. A single sealed win is the shape noise takes.
engineUses: simple moving average of true range (functions/api/check-signals.js)
backtestsUse: Wilder smoothing, which is what TradingView and MT5 call ATR
verdict: Neither ATR definition is established as better: engine minus backtests is 0.0116R in training, -0.0023R in validation and -0.0007R sealed, and the sign flips. What is NOT in doubt is that they differ: the engine's stops run 0.9% wider than every published measurement on this site assumes, so the backtests describe a slightly different system from the one that ships.
